as_written_in_papers.quote: Whole exome sequencing revealed a heterozygous c.212C>A missense mutation in exon 1 of the GFAP gene.

cases.statement: One carrier: a 51-year-old Indian man (heterozygous) with adult-onset AxD and tadpole brainstem atrophy.

people.label: patient
people.key_phenotypes: progressive spastic quadriparesis over 3 years; spastic dysarthria; urinary urgency and frequency; broken pursuit eye movements; T2 signal and atrophy of medulla and upper cervical cord (tadpole sign)

quotes.quote: A 51-year-old man presented with a 3-year history of weakness and stiffness of both upper and lower limbs with walking difficulties.
Subsequently, he developed slurring of speech and urinary disturbances in the form of urinary urgency and frequency.
On examination, he had spastic dysarthria with normal cognition.
He had broken pursuit eye movements with normal saccades.

Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain and spinal cord revealed a T2-hyperintense signal and atrophy of the medulla and upper cervical cord, giving rise to the classical “tadpole sign” [Figure 1a–c].

phenotype_specificity.statement: Adult-onset pattern (spasticity, bulbar speech, tadpole sign); routine laboratory tests normal. No other genetic testing or exclusion of other genes is described beyond whole exome sequencing; no family history of similar illness.

quotes.quote: Routine laboratory parameters like complete blood count, blood sugar, vitamin B12, renal function tests, and liver function tests were normal.
Based on the clinical and MRI findings, AOAD was considered.
He did not have any family history of similar illness.

segregation.statement: No relatives tested; parents deceased; no family history of similar illness.

quotes.quote: Parental testing to confirm the pathogenicity of the variant could not be done, as his parents are not alive.
He did not have any family history of similar illness.

de_novo.statement: Parents not tested (both deceased); de novo status unknown.

quotes.quote: Parental testing to confirm the pathogenicity of the variant could not be done, as his parents are not alive.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense per the paper; the protein change is not stated in the paper, and p.(Ala71Glu) is the batch's prediction from NM_002055.5. No mechanism statement in the paper.

quotes.quote: Whole exome sequencing revealed a heterozygous c.212C>A missense mutation in exon 1 of the GFAP gene.

computational_predictions.statement: In-silico prediction reported only as 'possibly damaging'; no tool named.

quotes.quote: The in silico prediction of the variant is possibly damaging.

authors_classification.statement: Variant of uncertain significance by ACMG; described as novel and not previously described.

quotes.quote: The GFAP variation in our patient is classified as a variant of uncertain significance based on the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) classification.
It is a novel variant and has not been described previously.

concerns: No transcript and no protein change stated in the paper; the protein p.(Ala71Glu) is predicted only from the batch HGVS on NM_002055.5. The panel should confirm the transcript the lab used.
Short letter-format report; no description of exome filtering or other variants found.
notes_for_panel: Single adult case, parents deceased, no segregation or functional data.
